Implementation Plan

## Plan: make the CI failure on PR #8960 (`ai/issue-8953`) pass again

**Planning ref:** `ai/issue-8953` at `ae0e7c293fc6a262d537792a083cf9627e8ad850`. The integration branch matches (`Integration branch mismatch: false`).

### Root cause (from the traceback comment and the code)
The comment on this issue settles the triage's open question. The failing step is "Merge-train and gh_helpers rate-limit tests", shard `rest`. One test failed: `tests/test_gh_retry_stdout_isolation.py::test_closed_reader_does_not_rerun_a_successful_command` (`1 failed, 239 passed`). It was not a timeout, and it was not one of the #8953 tests.

The test pipes 1 MiB of `gh_retry` output into `head -c 1`. It expects `gh_retry` to report a non-zero status because the reader closed the pipe. The `ubuntu-26.04` runners use uutils (Rust) coreutils. The diagnostics in the log show `cat_head=0 0`: the Rust `head -c 1` reads all of its input before it exits. The writer therefore never sees a closed pipe, and the test gets `rc=0`. The same diagnostics show `cat_true=141 0`: a reader that exits at once (`true`) does produce SIGPIPE/EPIPE. `gh_retry` in `scripts/gh_helpers.sh` behaves correctly. The fault is in the test's assumption about the runner's tools.

**Conflict noted:** The issue body lists `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, `.github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml`, `tests/test_review_dispatch_default_branch.py` and `tests/test_conflict_dispatch_active_run_visibility.py` as likely candidates. None of them is involved. The failing test was not changed by PR #8960 either; the runner image changed under it.

**The default branch already has the fix.** `git diff isolated-base -- tests/test_gh_retry_stdout_isolation.py` shows one hunk only. In `isolated-base`, the test pipes into `| true` instead of `| head -c 1 > /dev/null`, carries a comment explaining the Rust `head` behaviour, and adds the failure-only helper `_closed_pipe_diagnostics(tmp_path, env)` to its assertion message. `scripts/gh_helpers.sh` is identical between the branch and `isolated-base`. This branch was cut before that fix, so the fix is not on the planning ref and there is still work to do.

## Files likely to change
- `tests/test_gh_retry_stdout_isolation.py`

## Acceptance

## Functions or modules to implement
In `tests/test_gh_retry_stdout_isolation.py`, make the file byte-identical to its `isolated-base` version (`git show isolated-base:tests/test_gh_retry_stdout_isolation.py`). That hunk is the only difference, and copying it exactly means the later main → branch merge is a no-op for this file.
1. In `test_closed_reader_does_not_rerun_a_successful_command`:
   - Change the pipeline body from `"gh_retry gh api repos/o/r | head -c 1 > /dev/null\n"` to `"gh_retry gh api repos/o/r | true\n"`.
   - Replace the 3-line comment with the default branch's 8-line comment, which explains the Rust `head` behaviour on `ubuntu-26.04`.
   - Extend the assertion message tuple to `(rc_line, result.stderr, _closed_pipe_diagnostics(tmp_path, env))`.
   - Keep `_calls(tmp_path) == 1`, `rc_line != "rc=0"` and the leftover-temp-file assertion unchanged. The contract is not weakened.
2. Add the module-level helper `_closed_pipe_diagnostics(tmp_path: Path, env: dict[str, str]) -> str`, verbatim from `isolated-base`, directly after the test. On failure it reports `type -a cat head`, the tool versions, the signal masks and the PIPESTATUS of the cat/head/true probes. The name is new in this file and does not collide with anything else.

No production code changes.

## Data structures affected
None.

## API or interface changes
None. The change is test-only, so no changelog fragment and no agents.d fragment are needed.

## Decisions
### D1 — Port the default-branch test fix instead of changing gh_retry
- Chosen: copy `isolated-base`'s version of the test file into `ai/issue-8953`.
- Alternatives considered: change `gh_retry` in `scripts/gh_helpers.sh` so it returns non-zero under the Rust `head`; mark the test xfail or skip it on uutils; re-run CI and treat the failure as flaky.
- Why: `gh_retry` is correct. The reader just never closes its end of the pipe early. The failure is deterministic on `ubuntu-26.04` runners, so a re-run will not fix it. Skipping would weaken the assertion, which the triage forbids. Copying main's exact text avoids a future merge conflict.

### D2 — Do not port the other default-branch-only ci.yml changes
- Chosen: leave the actionlint cache change (#9056) and the `sf_now_ms` EPOCHREALTIME change out of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
- Alternatives considered: sync all of `ci.yml` with `isolated-base`.
- Why: neither change is involved in this failure. Pulling them in widens scope (§9) and would also need `tests/test_ci_actionlint_cache.py`. They arrive through the normal main → branch merge.

## Security considerations
- No trust boundary, endpoint, secret or workflow permission is touched. The change only affects a pytest file run in CI.
- The diagnostics helper runs local probes (`cat`, `head`, `/proc/self/status`) on a temp file it creates itself. It prints no environment values, so no secret can leak through the assertion message.
- No money-handling surfaces are involved.

## Risks and edge cases
- `| true` could in theory exit before `gh_retry` starts writing. That is the intended case: the 1 MiB replay is far larger than a pipe buffer, so the write must hit EPIPE or SIGPIPE. The CI diagnostics confirm it (`cat_true=141`).
- On GNU coreutils runners, `| true` also yields a non-zero writer status, so the test stays portable.
- Main may change this file again before the branch merges main. Copying it verbatim keeps any conflict trivial.
- The issue named other candidate files. They are ruled out by the traceback, and the implementer should not touch them.

## Testing considerations
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_gh_retry_stdout_isolation.py -q`: the whole module should pass.
- Before the change, the target test fails on hosts with uutils `head`, which is the reported `rc=0`. On GNU hosts it passes both before and after.
- CI: the `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` job's "Merge-train and gh_helpers rate-limit tests" step (`ci.yml:882` lists the module) and the aggregate `lint` job should go green.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends test_closed_reader_does_not_rerun_a_successful_command
Scope-mode justification: The failure is one test whose reader process does not close the pipe early on the new runner image. The default branch already fixed it in exactly this test, together with a failure-only diagnostics helper. Porting that hunk verbatim restores CI on `ai/issue-8953` without changing `gh_retry` or weakening any assertion. The complete option (test change plus helper) costs about 25 extra lines over the bare one-line reader swap, adds no dependency and no interface. Following the "Boil the Lake" rule and the §6 order (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), it is the chosen option: it keeps the file identical to main and improves the failure diagnostics. The unrelated `ci.yml` drift is left to the normal main merge.
